title: Microsoft 365 Business Basic vs Standard vs Premium: India Price & Feature Comparison
excerpt: Compare Microsoft 365 Business Basic, Standard and Premium in India: feature table, price per user, the 300-seat cap and who should choose which plan.
body:
Business Basic, Standard and Premium run the same core service: Exchange email on your own domain, Teams, SharePoint and 1 TB of OneDrive per user. The differences are the desktop Office applications (not in Basic) and the security and device management layer (only in Premium). Pick the lowest plan that covers what each person actually does, and mix plans inside one tenant where it makes sense.

## The three plans at a glance

| | Business Basic | Business Standard | Business Premium |
|---|---|---|---|
| Price per user per year, excluding GST | {{price:microsoft-365-business-basic}} | {{price:microsoft-365-business-standard}} | {{price:microsoft-365-business-premium}} |
| Price including 18% GST | {{gst:microsoft-365-business-basic}} | {{gst:microsoft-365-business-standard}} | {{gst:microsoft-365-business-premium}} |
| Installed Word, Excel, PowerPoint, Outlook | No | Yes, up to five devices per user | Yes, up to five devices per user |
| Web and mobile Office apps | Yes | Yes | Yes |
| Business email on your own domain | 50 GB mailbox | 50 GB mailbox | 50 GB mailbox |
| Teams meetings, chat and shared channels | Yes | Yes | Yes |
| OneDrive storage per user | 1 TB | 1 TB | 1 TB |
| SharePoint team sites | Yes | Yes | Yes |
| Intune device management and remote wipe | No | No | Yes |
| Entra ID P1: conditional access, self-service password reset | No | No | Yes |
| Defender for Office 365 Plan 1 (safe attachments, safe links) | No | No | Yes |
| Azure Information Protection labelling | No | No | Yes |
| Windows 11 Business upgrade rights | No | No | Yes, from a qualifying Windows Pro licence |
| Seat maximum | 300 | 300 | 300 |

These are annual commitment prices billed yearly, shown excluding GST unless the row says otherwise. They are tentative until a written quotation fixes them. Monthly and multi-year terms can be quoted on request.

## The 300-seat cap, explained properly

The three Business plans share one limit: 300 seats in a tenant, counted across Basic, Standard and Premium combined. It is not 300 of each. Mixing plans does not get you past it, and there is no override or grace allowance.

If you expect to cross 300 users within a couple of years, plan the move to an Enterprise plan before you need it. Moving under deadline pressure at a renewal is the expensive way to do it. Our [Microsoft 365 licensing guide for Indian businesses](/blog/microsoft-365-licensing-guide-for-indian-businesses) covers that transition and how the Enterprise plans differ.

## Business Basic: who it suits

Basic gives you hosted services without installed desktop apps. Staff work in the browser or on the mobile apps, or already have Office licensed another way.

Choose it for:

- Frontline, field and shop-floor staff who read mail, join Teams calls and open the odd document
- Branch or warehouse users in Indian retail and logistics businesses who share devices
- Companies that already own desktop Office (for example volume licences) and only want email, Teams and storage
- Part-time or seasonal staff you add and remove as demand changes

The limitation shows up quickly with anyone who lives in Excel. The web version handles most everyday work but not everything a finance team does with a heavy workbook. If someone complains within a week, they were not a Basic user. The detail is in our [Business Basic price and plan guide](/blog/microsoft-365-business-basic-price-in-india).

## Business Standard: who it suits

Standard is the common default. It adds installed Word, Excel, PowerPoint and Outlook on up to five PCs or Macs, five tablets and five phones per user.

Choose it for:

- Office-based staff in finance, sales, HR, operations and administration
- Anyone exchanging tender documents, bids and financial models in prescribed formats with larger corporates or government departments
- Consultants and professionals who work offline on trains, flights or client sites
- Small firms that want one plan for nearly everyone

If you are unsure, Standard is the safe middle, because changing a user between plans later is generally a licensing change rather than a migration. The mechanics depend on the agreement the subscription sits under, so confirm before committing. See [what Business Standard includes and costs](/blog/microsoft-365-business-standard-price-in-india).

## Business Premium: who it suits

Premium has the same applications and services as Standard. It adds control. Intune manages devices, Entra ID P1 adds conditional access, Defender for Office 365 checks attachments and links, and Azure Information Protection labels and encrypts documents.

Choose it for:

- People who use personal phones for work mail and need a PIN requirement and remote wipe
- Finance approvers, directors and anyone who can authorise payments
- Staff handling client confidential data under contract, such as accounting, legal, architecture and engineering firms
- Companies that must show access control to an auditor, a large customer or a tender evaluator

Premium is a capability rather than a product that works on arrival. Switched on without configuration, it adds cost without adding protection. Read [Business Premium security you already own](/blog/microsoft-365-business-premium-security-you-already-own) and our [Standard versus Premium comparison](/blog/microsoft-365-business-standard-vs-business-premium) before deciding. Pricing context is in the [Business Premium price guide](/blog/microsoft-365-business-premium-price-in-india).

## Mixing plans: a sensible setup

Licences are assigned per user, so one tenant can hold all three plans. A typical 60-person firm might look like this:

| Group | People | Plan |
|---|---|---|
| Directors, finance approvers, client-data handlers | 10 | Premium |
| General office staff | 35 | Standard |
| Warehouse, reception and site staff | 15 | Basic |

You do not need to copy these numbers. The point is that risk and workload are uneven, so the spending should be too. The same logic appears on our [Microsoft 365 page](/microsoft-365), which recommends mixed estates over uniform ones.

One caution: conditional access policies and device policies apply to the people who hold the licences for them. If your Premium users are a minority, accounts without Premium protection are still reachable by attackers, so enforce basic multi-factor authentication for everybody.

## Features that are the same on all three

It helps to know what you are not paying extra for:

- A 50 GB mailbox on your own domain
- Teams meetings, chat and shared channels
- 1 TB of OneDrive per user
- SharePoint team sites and shared libraries
- Web and mobile versions of the Office applications
- Administration through the Microsoft 365 admin centre

So the cost question is never "email or no email". It is "desktop apps?" and then "security layer?".

## Common mistakes when picking a plan

1. **Buying Premium for everyone** because security sounds important, then configuring nothing.
2. **Buying Basic for people who need Excel** and then discovering the web version is not enough.
3. **Comparing only the per-seat figure** and ignoring what Premium may replace, such as a separate endpoint protection product, a mobile device management tool and an email security gateway.
4. **Forgetting the seat cap** until a renewal arrives.
5. **Assuming Premium includes Windows.** It includes upgrade rights from a qualifying Windows Pro licence. It does not license a bare machine. Our note on [Windows 11 Pro versus Enterprise](/blog/windows-11-pro-versus-enterprise-for-business) explains the distinction.
6. **Treating GST as a cost.** The invoice carries 18% GST, which a registered business can usually claim as input credit. See [GST input credit on software purchases](/blog/gst-input-credit-on-software-purchases).

## A quick way to decide

Ask these questions in order for each group of users:

1. Do they need installed Office apps? If no, Basic. If yes, go on.
2. Do they use personal phones, handle client confidential files, or must you prove access control? If yes, Premium. If no, Standard.
3. Will your tenant exceed 300 users soon? If yes, request a quotation that includes Enterprise options.

## Three worked examples

**A 12-person accounting practice.** Everyone uses Excel daily and handles client financial data on laptops and personal phones. Standard is the floor for all twelve, with Premium for the partners and anyone holding client bank details, or for everyone if you cannot separate them. Basic is a false economy here.

**A 120-person manufacturer.** Twenty people work in offices, forty are supervisors and engineers who use desktop Office, and sixty are on the shop floor with shared terminals. A sensible split is Standard for the office and engineering groups, Basic for the shop floor, and Premium for finance and the owner's office. Total headcount is well inside the 300-seat cap.

**A 280-person services company growing fast.** It has room for only about twenty more seats. Buy for today, but ask for a quotation that shows the Enterprise route in parallel, so the move happens on your timetable.

## What to do before you buy

Take twenty minutes to list your users in three columns: who needs installed apps, who handles sensitive data or uses a personal phone, and who is temporary. That list is the whole quotation request. Add any existing perpetual Office licences, because some users may not need the installed apps from the subscription, and note whether anything depends on a Windows Pro upgrade. Send it through the [enquiry form](/enquiry) and the quotation will show the seat mix against each plan, with GST on the invoice.

## How to buy

Both the annual price and the number of seats matter at quotation time. Seats can be added during the term, while reductions take effect at renewal, so start with the seats you need today. Browse the plans on [Basic](/products/microsoft-365-business-basic), [Standard](/products/microsoft-365-business-standard) and [Premium](/products/microsoft-365-business-premium), or [request a quotation](/enquiry) with your headcount by role. We issue a GST invoice on every order and help with activation and seat assignment.

faqs.question: Which Microsoft 365 Business plan is best for a small office in India?
faqs.answer: For most desk-based teams Business Standard is the sensible default, because it adds installed Word, Excel, PowerPoint and Outlook to the hosted services. Choose Basic for frontline staff who work in a browser, and Premium for people handling sensitive data or using personal phones for work mail.

faqs.question: What is the seat limit on Business Basic, Standard and Premium?
faqs.answer: The three Business plans share a limit of 300 seats per tenant, counted across all three plans combined. There is no override. If you expect to pass 300 users, ask for a quotation that includes Enterprise plans so you can plan the move in advance.

faqs.question: Does Business Premium include Windows 11?
faqs.answer: No. It includes Windows 11 Business upgrade rights, which require a device already licensed with a qualifying Windows Pro edition. It does not license a bare machine. Check your existing Windows licences before assuming the upgrade rights apply.

faqs.question: Can I mix Basic, Standard and Premium in one tenant?
faqs.answer: Yes. Licences are assigned per user, so one tenant can hold all three plans, subject to the shared 300-seat cap. Put the people who need installed apps or stronger security on the higher plans and leave the rest on Basic or Standard.

faqs.question: Are the prices shown inclusive of GST?
faqs.answer: The main prices are shown excluding GST, and a separate figure including 18% GST is given in the table. A written quotation fixes the final amount. A GST-registered business can usually claim input credit on the GST, and every order carries a GST invoice.

faqs.question: Can I change plans or add seats during the term?
faqs.answer: Seats can generally be added at any point in the term, while reductions take effect at the annual renewal date. Moving users between plans depends on the agreement the subscription sits under, so confirm the mechanics before committing. Ask for a quotation if you need monthly or multi-year terms.
